problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z=3 \\ y+5z=-8 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4)=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4)=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$
